target_customer: Backend developers and teams building low-latency distributed apps (game servers, chat, web backends)
problem: Building fault-tolerant, highly concurrent servers is hard in mainstream languages; Lunatic offers Erlang-style lightweight processes on WebAssembly so any language can use them.
business_model: Open source runtime with planned paid hosting or managed platform (no pricing found)

founders.name: Bernard Kolobara
founders.background_notes: Built cluster monitoring tools at CERN; created the Lunatic runtime and runs communities around an open source ledger project.

founders.name: Hrvoje Bandov
previous_startups: Amodo (insurance tech, system architect, outcome not checked)
founders.background_notes: Contractor on backend projects including a real-time multiplayer game platform.

competitors.name: Wasmtime and Wasmer
competitors.what: General purpose WebAssembly runtimes that Lunatic builds on or competes with
competitors.traction_then: Open source projects with ongoing releases
competitors.funding_then: Wasmer venture backed; Wasmtime from the Bytecode Alliance

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a distributed, supervised process runtime on WebAssembly was systems-level work for a two-person team; the project was fully rewritten in July 2021 on Wasmtime async support.

defensibility.rationale: Open source licensing and big-company runtimes meant little structural protection; adoption depended on community mindshare.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger WebAssembly platforms kept shipping; no source shows Lunatic being acquired or copied directly.

market_need_then: Interest in WebAssembly beyond browsers was rising in 2020 and 2021 and Erlang-style concurrency had a loyal following, but a commercial buyer for a new runtime was unproven.

branding.name_origin: Founder says the project began as a programming language compiling to Lua, hence the name Lunatic; he kept the name through later pivots to a VM and runtime.

identity.logo: Moon logo, a nod to the Lua origin per the founder interview

branding.community_and_virality: Open source community on GitHub, Discord and Product Hunt (launched March 2021)

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable pun on Lua, but 'Lunatic' also carries negative connotations and the brand reached mostly the developer niche.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Lunatic as inactive, yet the website still loads with a 2023 footer and no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. A two-person team faced established runtimes from well-funded platforms and had no verified funding beyond YC, but no source states why activity stopped, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Directory status is Inactive but exit type is unknown because no shutdown evidence was found. Funding: Village.ai shows a seed round from Y Combinator without amount; Crunchbase page looked unreliable; no rounds recorded. Competitors are from undated or later comparison pages, so they are only approximate as of 2021.
